## Season so far

Emmett Johnson has been a low-usage depth back for most of the year. Through 8 games he has 53.8 points, 6.7 per game, on a 27% snap share and a 9% opportunity share. Weeks 1–7 were thin: 1.5 to 7.8 points, with 0 to 8 carries a game and nothing over 3 targets after Week 2. Week 8 was the only big game. He scored 22.8 on five catches for 128 yards and a touchdown, but it came on one carry and a 19% snap share, so it was mostly a few long plays. Week 9 was a more useful sign: 6 carries for 34 yards, a rushing TD and 2 red-zone carries, for 9.4 points.

## Usage and efficiency

The season line is 26 carries for 111 yards (4.3 per carry) and 16 targets for 237 yards (14.8 per target). The per-target figure is inflated by that one Week 8 game. Over the last 4 games the numbers are better: 9.6 points per game, 10 carries at 5.5 per carry, and 11 targets, up from 9% to 9% share but a bit more efficient. Snap share is flat at 26% against 27% for the season, so the role has not grown. Red-zone work is small, with 4 carries and 1 target all year and nothing at the goal line. The Stat Hub touchdown check shows 2 TDs against 0.7 expected, so some of the scoring is above what his usage supports. His production has been real but not backed by volume.

## Health and situation

Kenneth Walker III is out with a groin injury, and Adam Schefter reports Johnson will be the Chiefs' RB1 against Atlanta. My web check did not find independent confirmation of that, so treat the Schefter report as the source. Walker has a 42% opportunity share and a 74% snap share over the last 4 games, and Johnson is the clear next man at 9% and 26%. Groin strains usually cost a back one to three weeks, and re-aggravation is common when they return, so Walker's timeline is worth watching. Jaydn Ott (hamstring, questionable) is at 2% of opportunities, and I could not verify his status. Brashard Smith is on IR. That leaves Johnson with no real competition for touches. Separately, I found that Mahomes and Xavier Worthy had minor injury reports this week, and both looked fine to play.

## Outlook

Johnson projects at 7.5 points per game over the 9 remaining games (71.0 total, bye in Week 5), but that assumes Walker's usual role. Without Walker the role is bigger. The 74% snap share and 39% opportunity share Walker held would not all go to Johnson, but a large part would. The next four matchups are Week 10 @ ATL (easy), Week 11 vs ARI (neutral), Week 12 @ BUF (easy) and Week 13 @ LAR (tough). Week 10 is the best setup of the season. Treat him as a flex in half PPR this week, with a realistic range of about 8 to 15 points and a low floor if the Chiefs run a committee. If you can afford it, hold him through Walker's recovery, and if you are thin at RB, he is worth a waiver add. Go back to bench status once Walker returns.
